To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tropism of human immunodeficiency viruses is stable during 2 year of structured treatment interruptions.
the coreceptor tropism of HIV-1 does not change significantly after 2 year of STI.
the HIV tropism of the majority of patients remained stable during 24 months of structured treatment interruptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the HIV-1 coreceptor usage in a small cohort of patients who were treated with intermittent HAART for 2 years.
the impact of short-term uncontrolled virus exposure on coreceptor tropism in a small group of HIV-infected subjects.
the impact of short periods of uncontrolled virus replication during STIs on HIV coreceptor tropism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coreceptor switch in HIV is not influenced by short-term uncontrolled viral replication during STIs.
the coreceptor switch in HIV-1 is not a common phenomenon during 2 year of uncontrolled viral exposure in HAART responder patients.
HIV tropism is a stable phenotype and that no change occurs during 2  years of uncontrolled virus replication.

the tropism of HIV is not affected during 2 year of STI in HIV-1-infected individuals.

the HIV coreceptor tropism is stable over time in the majority of patients.
